claim: Multi-agent collaboration increases goal success rate relative to single-agent approaches in multi-step tasks.

claim: An extreme learning machine-based PDE solver that uses a fixed random input layer and linear least squares output has lower computational cost than a physics-informed neural network that employs backpropagation.
falsifier: On a linear PDE benchmark, measure the wall-clock training time of an ELM-based solver (fixed random input, least-squares output) and a PINN (gradient-based training); the ELM-based solver should complete in less time.

exclusions: limited to the reported comparison (BPIELM vs PINN) and experimental conditions (Poisson, advection, diffusion equations)

title: Using an extreme learning for computational cost
